entities.name: Publius Cornelius Rufinus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Cornelius Rufinus was a prominent Roman politician and general of the third century BC.

Born in Italy around 340 BCE, Rufinus rose to prominence during the tumultuous period of the late Republic, serving as consul in 322 BCE and later commander of the Roman army in Asia Minor. His military campaigns against the Seleucid Empire earned him recognition among his contemporaries.

Rufinus' significance lies in his role as a key figure in the transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire under Augustus Caesar, whom he supported during the power struggle that followed Julius Caesar's assassination.

Despite his important position, Rufinus' life remains somewhat shadowed by historical records, and his legacy has largely been overshadowed by more prominent figures of the time.

A testament to his enduring influence can be seen in the many inscriptions and coins bearing his name, which have helped scholars reconstruct his life and achievements with greater precision.
